problem: Given that $n\ge 2$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(n-1)^{2}\,(n-1)!}{(n-2)!}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Variable Expression Containing a Quotient With Many Factorials
examples.problem: Given that $k \geq 1$ is an integer, simplify $\dfrac {k^2(k - 1)!} {k!}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we notice that 

$$
k! = k \cdot (k-1)!
$$

So, we can simplify the numerator as follows:

$$
k^2 (k-1)! = k \cdot \underbrace{k \cdot (k-1)!}_{k!} = k \cdot k!
$$

Then, we cancel the $k!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac {k^2(k - 1)!} {k!} 
&= \dfrac {k \cdot k!} {k!}\[5pt]
&= \dfrac {k \cdot \cancel{k!}} {\cancel{k!}} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {k} {1} \[5pt]
&= k
	}
$$

feedback.problem: Given that $k\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(k+2)!}{(k-1)!}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
(k+2)!=(k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k\cdot (k-1)!
$$

Then, we cancel the $(k-1)!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(k+2)!}{(k-1)!} & =\frac{(k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k\cdot (k-1)!}{(k-1)!} \\  & =\frac{(k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k\cdot \cancel{(k-1)!}}{\cancel{(k-1)!}} \\  & =k(k+1)(k+2)\end{aligned}
$$
